answer: At most 3 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a signal tag. The dawn cap is enforced at intake and jetty exposes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a fleet in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because every identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 22 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
